info.name: Vicinia — Full API (Stage 0-16)
info.description:
Every gateway-routed endpoint across all 16 services, current through Stage 16 (observability). Run 'Auth > Signup' first for a plain customer — its test script auto-captures accessToken/refreshToken/userId, which every customer-scoped request below reuses automatically. Each of Merchant/Delivery has its own role-specific signup request at the top of its folder for the same reason.

ADMIN BOOTSTRAP: there's no self-registration for ADMIN (auth-service rejects it, 400) and no admin bootstrap flow exists yet (a known, documented gap — see BUILD_TRACKER.md Stage 3's notes) — sign up a plain CUSTOMER, grant the ADMIN role directly via SQL (INSERT INTO user_roles ... SELECT ... FROM roles WHERE name='ADMIN', against auth_db), then log in again and paste the resulting accessToken into the adminAccessToken collection variable by hand.

Recommended run order for a full, realistic order lifecycle: Auth > Signup (customer) -> Merchant > Signup+Apply -> (admin-approve the merchant) -> Merchant > Update Store Profile/Hours + Go Live -> Catalog > Create Product (admin, or request+approve as merchant) -> Inventory > Create Listing -> Cart > Add Item -> Payment > Top Up Wallet -> Order > Place Order -> Merchant Orders > Accept/Ready -> Delivery > Signup+Go Online -> Tasks > Accept/Picked Up/Delivered -> Review > Create Review, Settlement > My Settlement Entries.

variable.description: Set by hand — see the 'ADMIN BOOTSTRAP' note in this collection's description.
The Merchant application's own id (from Apply as Merchant) — distinct from merchantUserId.

request.description: role is optional (defaults to CUSTOMER) and must be one of CUSTOMER, MERCHANT, DELIVERY_PARTNER — ADMIN cannot self-register (400). Returns 409 if the email is already registered.
200 with tokens on success, 401 on wrong password or unknown email.
Rotates the refresh token — the old one becomes invalid the instant this succeeds (re-running this exact request twice in a row will 401 on the second try, by design).
Blacklists the current access token and revokes the refresh token. Any request using {{accessToken}} after this will 401 — re-run Login to get a fresh one.

Always returns 200 with the same message, whether or not the email exists (no account enumeration). Since notification-service doesn't exist yet, the actual reset token is only visible in auth-service's own log output (logs/auth-service.log) — copy it into the resetToken variable to test Reset Password below.
One-time use — a second attempt with the same token 401s. Also revokes all existing refresh sessions for that user.
404 for a few seconds right after Signup — the profile is created asynchronously by user-service consuming the user.registered Kafka event, not synchronously by the signup call itself.
Creates a MERCHANT-role account — separate from the customer 'Signup' in the Auth folder. Run this once before anything else in this folder.
Creates the merchant application in PENDING_REVIEW. An ADMIN must approve it (see Admin > Approve Merchant) before /me/go-live will work.

request.description: latitude/longitude are required before /me/ready (merchant marking an order ready for pickup, see Merchant Orders) will work — delivery-service needs them to search for a nearby partner.
Required before /me/go-live — a store can't go live without published hours.
Requires the merchant to already be ADMIN-approved (status ONBOARDING) with hours set. On success, status becomes LIVE and the store is orderable.
Public — no Authorization header needed (api-gateway's public-paths). Only returns LIVE stores.
Requires MERCHANT_APPROVE (seeded onto ADMIN). See the 'Admin Bootstrap' note at the collection root for how to get an admin token — there's no self-registration for ADMIN.
Transitions PENDING_REVIEW -> ONBOARDING. Uses the merchantId captured by 'Apply as Merchant' (the application's own id, not the owner's userId).
Orders auto-created here from order.confirmed Kafka events — place a real order first (see Order folder) as this same merchant's customer.
order-service double-hops CONFIRMED -> MERCHANT_ACCEPTED -> PREPARING on success.
400 StoreLocationNotSetException if latitude/longitude aren't set (see Update My Store Profile). Publishes order.ready, which delivery-service consumes to search for a nearby online partner.
Public — both q and category are optional filters.
Lands in PENDING_REVIEW — an admin must approve it (see Admin > Approve Product) before it's usable in a listing.

Public — every merchant currently selling this product, for a product detail page's 'available at' list.

request.description: Every field optional — a partial update, same convention as inventory-service's UpdateListingRequest.
Wallet is auto-provisioned from the user.registered Kafka event right after signup — may 404 for a second or two immediately after Signup.
Needed before placing a WALLET-method order in the Order folder.

Reads the caller's own cart (must be non-empty, single-merchant, see Cart folder), reserves inventory, debits the wallet synchronously. paymentMethod defaults to WALLET if omitted; couponCode is optional.

exec: if (body.id !== undefined && body.id !== null) pm.collectionVariables.set('orderId', body.id);

request.description: Order lands in PAYMENT_PENDING with a real razorpayOrderId/razorpayKeyId in the response — resolves to CONFIRMED only once Razorpay's webhook fires (asynchronous by nature, see payment-service's RazorpayWebhookController). Requires real Razorpay test-mode credentials in .env.
Only allowed pre-DELIVERED (CREATED/CONFIRMED/PREPARING -> CANCELLED); releases the inventory reservation and triggers an async refund via order.cancelled.
Auto-provisions a DeliveryPartner row (status OFFLINE) via the user.registered Kafka event — nothing else to set up.
Writes into Redis GEO (key delivery:partners:online) so order.ready's nearest-partner search can find this partner. Use coordinates near whatever merchant location you set in the Merchant folder.

Only works once delivery-service has actually assigned this order's task to this partner (via order.ready + a nearby GEO search) — mark the order ready first (Merchant > Merchant Orders > Mark Order Ready).
Cycles the task back to PENDING_ASSIGNMENT with this partner excluded from the next search, rather than a terminal REJECTED status — the order still needs delivering.
order-service double-hops DELIVERY_ASSIGNED -> OUT_FOR_DELIVERY -> DELIVERED on success, then publishes order.delivered (settlement-service's trigger).
Populated from 4 consumed Kafka events (user.registered, order.confirmed, payment.failed, inventory.low) — a welcome notification should already be here right after Signup.

403 unless this exact user has a DELIVERED order containing this productId (checked live against order-service). 409 on a second review of the same product by the same user — one review per (user, product), enforced by a real unique index.
Computed live via a MongoDB aggregation, not a stored running average — {productId, averageRating, reviewCount}.
One entry per delivered order for this merchant (gross/commission/net) — see Delivery > Tasks > Mark Delivered to produce one.
Requires SETTLEMENT_MANAGE.
On-demand version of the scheduled daily job — groups every merchant's PENDING entries into one new Payout each (summing net, not gross).
On-demand version of the scheduled 30s tick — advances PENDING->PROCESSING immediately, and PROCESSING->PAID once the configured processing delay has passed.
